meta.comment: Interactive hotspots. (u,v) are NORMALISED poster coordinates: 0..1 from the TOP-LEFT corner of poster.jpg. They drive both the AR anchors (mapped onto the tracked image plane) and the on-screen Demo Mode. Tweak (u,v) to line each dot up with your printed poster.

hotspots.label: Geometry
hotspots.body: The computational domain is a closed rectangular water tank, about 7.5 cm tall, filled with water at 293 K. A small horizontal jet enters at mid-height. The warm jet is lighter than the surrounding water, so it rises and builds a vertical thermal layer.

hotspots.label: Mesh
hotspots.body: A structured mesh of small cubic cells (1 mm each) fills the tank. Regular cells keep the numerical scheme stable and let the cell-to-cell (C2C) shift maps of rCFD be defined cleanly on neighbouring faces.

hotspots.label: Boundary Conditions
hotspots.body: Inlet velocity (U = 0.02 m/s), inlet temperature (333 K warm until t = 315 s, then cold), and the laminar flow assumption define the scenario. With Re = U·D/ν ≈ 100 the jet stays laminar, so a laminar model fits better than turbulence closure.

hotspots.label: Results
hotspots.body: rCFD reproduces the CFD temperature field across the full 600 s at a small fraction of the cost. Buoyancy-driven recirculation vortices and the rising thermal layer are captured; the face-swap diffusion strength f_sd = 0.500 gives the lowest centre-of-gravity error.
